A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DBAE research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original DBAE experiments on downstream inference, reconstruction, disentanglement, and generation, with additional analyses and qualitative results in Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains original DBAE experiments and adds CIFAR-10 results, DiffuseVAE comparisons, additional reconstruction results, and an accelerator reproducibility experiment.

M1.justification: The encoder-decoder construction of z-dependent endpoints, h-transformed diffusion bridge, reconstruction and prior objectives, and separate latent-prior training remain unchanged. Expanded architecture descriptions, manipulation equations, and relocated algorithms document the existing procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds CIFAR-10 linear-probe evaluation in Table 9, extending the represented data beyond the previously evaluated attribute datasets. CelebA, FFHQ, LFW, CelebA-HQ, and LSUN Horse/Bedroom were already covered; additional reconstruction scores on these datasets mainly extend the reported results.

E2.justification: V2 adds DiffuseVAE as an evaluated comparator for linear-probe prediction and CelebA reconstruction in Tables 9–10. Comparator membership in the retained main experiments and sampling-step comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: Figure 4 changes the reported TC-coefficient sweep from {0, 0.04, 0.06, 0.1} to {0, 0.04, 0.1}. Added experiments introduce CIFAR-10 AUROC evaluation and testing across two accelerators. Existing training configuration tables remain unchanged; newly disclosed Table 2 sampler settings do not establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: V2 adds a reproducibility analysis testing whether DBAE-d reconstruction remains consistent between NVIDIA A100 and Intel Gaudi v2 hardware (Appendix D.4, Table 15). The TC sensitivity analysis is revised. Existing encoder-stochasticity, reconstruction-variation, sampling-step, and manipulation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V1 Table 3 explicitly states that results were evaluated five times; v2 removes that disclosure while retaining the reported ± values. This does not establish fewer evaluations. Five-evaluation averaging remains documented for linear probes, without a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds CIFAR-10 AUROC results (DBAE 0.836; DiffuseVAE 0.736), reconstruction comparisons, and hardware results in Tables 9–11 and 15. Table 1 changes DiffAE's FFHQ AP from 0.597 to 0.605. Table 3 changes DBAE TAD from 0.165±0.096 to 0.124±0.078 and DBAE+TC from 0.417±0.066 to 0.362±0.036. The accompanying TC sweep changes, limiting a same-setting interpretation of the regularized results.

T1.justification: V2 introduces comparative mutual-information bounds in Sections 3 and 4.3 and Appendix A.4. A new Theorem 2 and Appendix A.5 connect negative mutual information to LAE, replacing v1's optimal-score Corollary 2. The reconstruction and generative-modeling theorems are retained.

C1.justification: V1's abstract, introduction, and conclusion claim to resolve both Gaussian over-regularization and information splitting. V2 removes the over-regularization contribution and centers the paper on information splitting, computationally expensive endpoint inference, and inflexible dimensionality. The z-dependent bottleneck construction and principal empirical claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds a central explanation linking auxiliary encoders' endpoint/prior mismatch to unavoidable information leakage and interpreting LAE minimization as increasing mutual information. It also explains DiffuseVAE's performance through its VAE representation and random endpoint, while acknowledging mismatched CelebA cropping. The earlier generation fidelity/diversity limitation remains.

D1.justification: V2 adds DBAE and Gaudi implementation links. Appendix C.2 newly specifies Heun ODE sampling with 99 NFE for Table 2 SSIM/MSE and stochastic sampling with 998 NFE for LPIPS. These clarify existing results; most architecture, optimization, and training-budget details were already supplied in v1.

R1.justification: V2 adds Alemi et al. (2018) for the mutual-information argument and Pandey et al. (2022) for DiffuseVAE. It removes the implicit-optimal-prior citation supporting over-regularization and several generation-related citations. The main discussion of diffusion representation learning and parameterized forward diffusion remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries, and experimental explanations undergo extensive rewriting. V2 separates diffusion fundamentals from representation learning, introduces a dedicated motivation section, and reorganizes the method around mutual-information analysis. Retained tasks receive clearer mathematical and procedural explanations.

P2.justification: V2 adds four compact appendix tables and redraws Figure 4 with revised proportions, axis range, and coefficient labels. Algorithms 1–2 move into the main text, while the endpoint-inference cost table moves to the appendix. Other figures and sample galleries are retained within the revised conference layout.

improvement.justification: V2 improves exposition, comparison coverage, and reproducibility documentation. However, its central new mutual-information comparison cancels forward and inverse Dirac kernels in Appendix A.4.1, Eqs. (107)–(109), without justifying that cancellation or accounting for the ODE change-of-variables factor. This leaves an important gap in the added theoretical explanation. The empirical and documentation gains coexist with this new weakness, making the overall net quality change uncertain.
